pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


When you first start following Jesus, you have a lot of questions. That is normal. That is good. You are learning. You are growing. You are trying to understand this new life you have stepped into.


One of the questions new believers often ask is about the Old Testament. You read it and it feels strange. You read about God appearing in a burning bush. You read about a man wrestling with God. You read about a mysterious angel who seems to be God Himself. You read about four men in a fire. And you think, "What is going on here? Who is this?"


Here is something beautiful that many new believers do not know yet. Jesus was not a surprise. He was not a backup plan. He was not an afterthought. He was there all along. Before He was born in Bethlehem, He was showing up. He was appearing. He was walking. He was talking. He came close.


This book is for you. You are new to the faith. You are building your foundation. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 moments in the Old Testament where Jesus showed up before He was born. We are going to see that He has always wanted to be close. He has always wanted to be with His people. And He has always wanted to be with you.


This is not a difficult book. It is not a theology textbook. It is a simple journey. It is a journey through the ancient appearances of Jesus. And it will help you see that the God you are getting to know has been coming close for a very long time.



The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will see the Bible differently. You will see that it is one story. Not two. Not an Old Testament and a New Testament. One story about one God who wants to be close to His people.

pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the LORD God as he was walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden." - Genesis 3:8 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


This is the first time God appears in the Bible as a person. He is walking. In a garden. In the cool of the day. Adam and Eve hear His footsteps. They hide. They are afraid. They have sinned. But God does not stay away. He comes to them. He walks toward them. He calls out to them. This is the first appearance of Jesus in the Old Testament. He was walking. He was looking. He was coming close.


The Fulfillment


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


Jesus is the one who walked in the garden. He is the Word. He was with God in the beginning. And He came to the garden. And He walked. And He called. And He is the same one who came to earth as a baby. He came close. He always comes close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel like God is far away. You might feel like you have sinned too much. You might feel like you should hide. But the first story in the Bible tells a different story. God did not wait for Adam and Eve to clean up. He came to them. He walked toward them. He called to them. He is doing the same for you. He is not waiting for you to be perfect. He is walking toward you right now.


Faith Builder


Take a few minutes today and imagine God walking toward you. Not away from you. Toward you. Write down how that makes you feel.


The Prayer


God, thank you for coming close. Thank you for walking toward me. Thank you for not waiting for me to be perfect. Help me to stop hiding. Help me to come out and walk with you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 1: The God Who Walked in the Garden

pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground." - Genesis 18:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Three men came to Abraham's tent. One of them was God. Abraham did not know it at first. But he offered them food. He washed their feet. He made them a meal. And God sat at his table. God ate. God talked. God stayed. This is the second appearance of Jesus in the Old Testament. He was a guest. He was at the table. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person, and they with me." - Revelation 3:20


Jesus wants to eat with you. He wants to sit at your table. He wants to talk with you. He wants to stay. The tent meal was a preview. The table with Jesus is the reality. He is not just a God who watches from heaven. He is a God who wants to come in and sit down.


Why It Matters For You


You might think of God as distant. As somewhere up there. As someone who is not interested in your daily life. But the tent meal tells a different story. God wants to be with you. He wants to sit at your table. He wants to eat with you. He wants to be part of your ordinary life. Not just your Sunday life. Your Monday life. Your Tuesday life. Your dinner life.


Faith Builder


Set aside a few minutes today to sit quietly with God. Imagine Him at your table. Talk to Him. Tell Him about your day. Let Him be close.


The Prayer


Jesus, come to my table. Come and sit with me. I want you to be part of my everyday life. Not just my Sunday life. My Monday life. My dinner life. Stay with me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 2: The God at the Tent

pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in flames of fire from within a bush. Moses saw that though the bush was on fire it did not burn up." - Exodus 3:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was in the wilderness. He was a shepherd. He saw a bush on fire. But the bush did not burn up. The fire was real. The bush stayed green. Moses walked closer. And God spoke to him from the bush. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was in the fire. He was in the bush. He was speaking. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


Jesus is the burning bush. He is the fire in the bush. He is the presence in the person. The bush did not burn up. Jesus was not destroyed. The fire did not consume the bush. The grave did not consume Jesus. The bush was a preview. Jesus is the reality. He comes close. He speaks. He calls.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel like God is not speaking to you. You might feel like He is silent. But the burning bush tells a different story. God speaks. God calls. God shows up. Not always in a burning bush. Sometimes in a whisper. Sometimes in a verse. Sometimes in a friend. Sometimes in a moment of quiet. He is not silent. He is speaking. He wants to be close.


Faith Builder


Ask God to help you hear Him this week. Write down one way He might be speaking to you that you have not noticed before.


The Prayer


God, help me to hear you. Help me to notice when you are speaking. I do not want to miss you. You are close. You are not silent. Speak to me. I am listening. Amen.
pages.title: Day 3: The God in the Burning Bush

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"The angel of the LORD found Hagar near a spring in the desert... She gave this name to the LORD who spoke to her: 'You are the God who sees me.'" - Genesis 16:7, 13 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Hagar was a servant. She was running away. She was pregnant. She was alone. She was in the desert. And the angel of the Lord found her. He saw her. He spoke to her. He promised her a future. And she gave God a name. "You are the God who sees me." This is another appearance of Jesus. He sees. He comes. He speaks. He is close.


The Fulfillment


"But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us." - Romans 5:8


God saw us in our sin. God saw us in our lostness. God saw us in our desert. He did not wait for us to clean up. He came. He died. He found us. The God who saw Hagar is the Christ who sees you. He sees. He comes. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel invisible. You might feel like nobody sees you. You might feel like you are in the desert and no one knows. But the story of Hagar tells a different story. God sees you. He knows your name. He knows your pain. He knows your desert. You are not invisible to Him. He sees you. He comes to you.


Faith Builder


Write down one thing that makes you feel invisible or unseen. Then write this next to it: "The God who sees me." Say it out loud.


The Prayer


God, you see me. You see my desert. You see my pain. Thank you for seeing me. Thank you for coming to me. Thank you for knowing my name. I am not invisible to you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 4: The God Who Sees

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"So Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him till daybreak... Then the man said, 'Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome.'" - Genesis 32:24, 28 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Jacob was alone. He was scared. He was about to face his brother who wanted to kill him. And a man came. And they wrestled. All night. In the dark. In the dirt. And Jacob would not let go. The man was God. Jacob wrestled with God. And he walked away with a limp and a blessing. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was close. He was physical. He was real.


The Fulfillment


"But we see Jesus, who was made lower than the angels for a little while, now crowned with glory and honor because he suffered death." - Hebrews 2:9


Jacob wrestled a man. The man was God. God let Himself be grabbed. God let Himself be held. He could have broken free. He did not. This is a picture of Jesus. Jesus let Himself be grabbed, beaten, and held on a cross. He did not break free. He let Himself be held. For us. He came close. He let Himself be grabbed.


Why It Matters For You


You might be struggling. You might be angry. You might have questions you are afraid to ask. But the story of Jacob tells a different story. God is not scared of your struggle. God is not fragile. You can grab Him. You can hold on. You can wrestle. He will not break. He will bless you. He is close. He wants to be close. Even in the struggle.


Faith Builder


What are you struggling with right now? Write it down. Then write this: "I am holding on to God. I will not let go until He blesses me."


The Prayer


God, I am struggling. I am not going to let go. I am holding on to you. Even if I limp away, I am not letting go until you bless me. You are worth holding. You are worth the fight. Amen.
pages.title: Day 5: The God Who Wrestled

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"'Neither,' he replied, 'but as commander of the army of the LORD I have now come.' Then Joshua fell facedown to the ground in reverence." - Joshua 5:14 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Joshua was about to fight a huge battle. He was camped near Jericho. He looked up and saw a man. The man had a sword drawn. Joshua asked, "Are you for us or for our enemies?" The man said, "Neither. I am the commander of the army of the Lord." Joshua fell down and worshiped. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came with a sword. He came to lead. He came to fight. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"Then Jesus came to them and said, 'All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.'" - Matthew 28:18


The commander of the Lord's army has all authority. Jesus has all authority. The same figure. The same power. Before Jesus was born, He was standing on the road to Jericho with a sword. He is not just a helper. He is the commander. The battle is His. And He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be facing a battle right now. A big one. A scary one. You might be asking, "God, are you on my side?" But the real question is different. Is He your commander? He is not a side. He is the leader. Let Him lead. The battle is already His. And He is with you. He is close. He is fighting for you.


Faith Builder


What battle are you facing today? Write it down. Then write this: "The commander of the Lord's army is with me. The battle is His."


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the commander. I stop asking if you are on my side. I choose your side. Lead me. Fight for me. The battle is yours. I trust you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 6: The God with a Sword

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods." - Daniel 3:25 (Written around 530 B.C.)


Three men refused to bow to a golden statue. The king threw them into a furnace. It was so hot it killed the guards. But the king looked in and saw four men. Walking. In the fire. The fourth man looked like a god. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was in the fire. He was with His people. He was walking. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age." - Matthew 28:20


Jesus promised to be with us. Not to keep us out of the fire. To be in it. The fourth man in the fire is a picture of Jesus. He is the one who walks with us through the fire. He does not leave. He does not run. He stays. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be in a fire right now. A trial. A hard season. A loss. You might feel like you are burning up. But the story of the furnace tells a different story. You are not alone. There is a fourth man. He is walking with you. He is in the fire. He will not leave you. You will come out. And you will not even smell of smoke.


Faith Builder


Write down the fire you are in right now. Then write this: "The fourth man is in the fire with me. I am not alone."


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the fourth man. You are in the fire with me. Thank you for walking with me. Thank you for staying. Thank you for not leaving. I am not alone. I am not afraid. You are here. Amen.
pages.title: Day 7: The God in the Fire

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"Then the LORD spoke to Job out of the storm." - Job 38:1 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


Job lost everything. His children. His money. His health. He was in pain. He was angry. He asked God questions. And God answered. Not in a soft voice. In a whirlwind. The storm came. And God spoke. And Job got what he needed. He got God. This is another appearance of Jesus. He spoke. He showed up. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, 'Quiet! Be still!' Then the wind died down and it was completely calm." - Mark 4:39


Jesus spoke to a storm. He calmed the wind. He calmed the waves. The same voice that spoke to Job spoke to the sea. The same God. The same power. The same presence. He speaks. He calms. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might have questions for God. You might have pain. You might have anger. You might feel like you cannot ask. But the story of Job tells a different story. Job asked. And God showed up. Not with easy answers. With Himself. God is not scared of your questions. He is not scared of your pain. He wants to speak to you. He is close. He is in the storm.


Faith Builder


Write down one question you have for God. Do not be afraid to ask it. Then sit quietly and let Him be near.


The Prayer


God, I have questions. I have pain. I have anger. I am done pretending. Speak to me. Show up. Not with easy answers. With yourself. I need you more than I need answers. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: The God Who Spoke in the Storm

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"He had a dream in which he saw a stairway resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it." - Genesis 28:12 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Jacob was running away. He was scared. He was alone. He used a rock for a pillow. He fell asleep. And he dreamed. He saw a ladder. It reached from earth to heaven. Angels were going up and down. And God was at the top. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was at the top. He was the connection. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"He then added, 'Very truly I tell you, you will see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.'" - John 1:51


Jesus said the ladder was Him. He is the stairway. He is the connection. He is the way between heaven and earth. He is the path between God and man. The ladder was a picture. Jesus is the reality. He is the connection. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel disconnected from God. You might feel like there is a gap. You might feel like there is a distance. But the story of the ladder tells a different story. There is a connection. There is a way. There is a bridge. Jesus is the connection. You can come close. You can come up. He made a way.


Faith Builder


Write down one way you feel disconnected from God. Then write this: "Jesus is the ladder. He connects me to God. I can come close."


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the ladder. You are the stairway. You are the connection. Thank you for making a way between heaven and earth. Thank you for making a way between me and God. I am coming close. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The God on the Ladder

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"The angel of the LORD answered, 'Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding.'" - Judges 13:18 (Written around 1100 B.C.)


Manoah and his wife could not have children. An angel appeared to the woman. He promised a son. She ran to tell her husband. He prayed. He wanted to see the angel for himself. The angel came back. And Manoah asked his name. The angel said something strange. "Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding." This is another appearance of Jesus. He is the angel. He is God. He is close.


The Fulfillment


"No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is himself God and is in closest relationship with the Father, has made him known." - John 1:18


Jesus makes God known. But before Jesus, the Son was already making God known. The Word was not silent before Bethlehem. He was speaking. He was showing up. He was visiting. The Son was in the Old Testament. He was the angel. He was close.


Why It Matters For You


You might want to understand everything about God. You might want to know His name. You might want to figure Him out. But some things are beyond understanding. And that is okay. God has shown Himself. In Jesus. He is the visible presence. He is the one who makes God known. You do not have to understand everything. You just have to know Him. And He is close.


Faith Builder


Write down one thing about God you do not understand. Then write this: "I do not have to understand everything. I just have to know Him. He is close."


The Prayer


God, you are beyond understanding. Your name is a mystery. But you have shown yourself in Jesus. Thank you. Thank you for making yourself known. Thank you for the visible presence. I look at Jesus. I see you. I know you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: The God with the Secret Name

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"Mount Sinai was covered with smoke, because the LORD descended on it in fire. The smoke billowed up from it like smoke from a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled violently." - Exodus 19:18 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The people were at the bottom of the mountain. The mountain was on fire. Smoke was rising. The ground was shaking. A voice was speaking. The people were terrified. They begged Moses to speak to God for them. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came down. He spoke. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire... But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God." - Hebrews 12:18, 22


The mountain was terrifying. But we have not come to that mountain. We have come to a better one. The fire was real. But Jesus opened a different way. We do not stand at the bottom, scared. We come close. We come to God as a Father. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel like God is a mountain you cannot climb. Like He is up there and you are down here and the smoke is too thick. But the story of the mountain tells a different story. The fire was real. But Jesus came to bring you up the mountain. You do not have to stand far away anymore. You can come close. You can come to the Father. You can come near.


Faith Builder


Write down one way you feel far from God. Then write this: "Jesus brought me up the mountain. I can come close to the Father."


The Prayer


God, you are holy. I am not. Thank you that Jesus makes a way. Thank you that I do not have to stay at the bottom of the mountain, shaking. Bring me close. Let me come up. Let me see your face. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: The God on the Mountain

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle." - Exodus 40:34-35 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The cloud came down. It covered the tent. The glory filled the tabernacle. Moses could not even go in. The presence of God was so heavy. So real. So thick. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was in the cloud. He was in the glory. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The glory cloud came down on a tent. Jesus came down in flesh. The word "dwelling" here literally means "pitched his tent." Jesus is the new tent. He is the new cloud. He is the glory of God, walking. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might want to experience God's presence. You might feel like you are outside the tent, looking in. But the story of the cloud tells a different story. The glory cloud was scary. But Jesus brought the glory down to us. He came near. He filled a human body. He can fill you. He is close.


Faith Builder


Set aside a few quiet minutes today. Ask God to fill you with His presence. Then sit still and let Him be near.


The Prayer


God, fill me with your presence. I do not want to stand outside, looking in. I want to know your glory. Thank you that Jesus brought your glory down to me. Fill me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The God in the Cloud

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"The angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him... When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, it turned off the road into a field." - Numbers 22:22-23 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Balaam was a prophet. He was on his way to curse God's people. He was riding a donkey. The donkey saw something Balaam could not. An angel. Standing in the road. With a drawn sword. The donkey stopped. Balaam beat it. And then the donkey spoke. This is another appearance of Jesus. He stood in the road. He opposed the wrong path. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"While they were going out, they met a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the cross." - Matthew 27:32


On the way to the cross, another man was pulled in. Simon of Cyrene carried the cross. He did not choose it. It was forced on him. The angel stood in the road. He opposed the wrong path. Jesus stood in the road of our sin. He took the sword. He took the curse. He stood in our place. He was close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be on a road right now. A road you should not be on. And God might be standing in it. Sometimes the thing that stops you is the thing that saves you. The donkey was smarter than the prophet. Listen. God may be standing in your road. He is not trying to ruin your journey. He is trying to save it. He is close.


Faith Builder


Is there a road you are on that you know you should not be on? Write it down. Ask God to help you turn around.


The Prayer


God, thank you for standing in my road. Thank you for the warnings. Help me to see. Help me to listen. You are not trying to ruin my journey. You are trying to save it. I will turn. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The God in the Road

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"After the earthquake came a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came a gentle whisper." - 1 Kings 19:12 (Written around 900 B.C.)


Elijah was scared. He had just won a huge victory. Then a queen threatened him. He ran. He hid in a cave. He was depressed. He wanted to die. And God came to him. Not in the wind. Not in the earthquake. Not in the fire. In a gentle whisper. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came in the whisper. He came in the quiet. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


God showed up in a whisper. Then He showed up in a baby. Not in a palace. In a stable. Not in the loud. In the quiet. God is not always in the loud things. He is in the small things. He is in the quiet. He is in the person. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be looking for God in the big things. In the loud things. In the dramatic things. But the story of Elijah tells a different story. He is in the quiet. He is in the whisper. He is in the small. He is in the person. He is close. Listen. He is speaking. Not in the earthquake. In the stillness. Be still. Hear Him.


Faith Builder


Find a quiet place today. No music. No phone. Just you and God. Sit for five minutes in the silence. Listen.


The Prayer


God, help me to hear the whisper. I am looking for the big things. I am waiting for the loud things. But you are in the quiet. Speak to me in the silence. I am listening. I am still. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The God in the Whisper

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple." - 2 Chronicles 7:1 (Written around 950 B.C.)


Solomon built the temple. It was beautiful. It was huge. It was the house of God. And when it was finished, Solomon prayed. He asked God to fill it. And fire came down. From heaven. And the glory filled the temple. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came down. He filled the temple. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"Don't you know that you yourselves are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in your midst?" - 1 Corinthians 3:16


We are the temple. God lives in us. The fire is in us. The glory is in us. The temple was a picture. The Spirit in us is the reality. The fire that filled the temple fills us. The glory that filled the temple fills us. He is close. He is in us.


Why It Matters For You


You might not know this yet. But you are the temple now. If you follow Jesus, the Spirit lives in you. You are the house of God. The fire is in you. The glory is in you. The presence is in you. You do not have to go to a building to find God. He is in you. He is close. He is closer than your own breath.


Faith Builder


Put your hand on your chest. Take a deep breath. Say out loud, "God lives in me. I am His temple."


The Prayer


God, thank you that I am your temple. Thank you that the fire fills me. Thank you that the glory fills me. Fill me with your presence. I am your house. I am your fire. I am your glory. Amen.
pages.title: Day 15: The God in the Temple

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"Suddenly the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. The king watched the hand as it wrote." - Daniel 5:5 (Written around 530 B.C.)


A king was having a party. He was mocking God. He was using the sacred cups from the temple. And then he saw it. A hand. Writing on the wall. The king was terrified. His knees knocked. His face went pale. This is another appearance of Jesus. He wrote. He spoke. He showed up. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"But Jesus bent down and started to write on the ground with his finger." - John 8:6


A hand wrote on a wall. A finger wrote on the ground. When the woman caught in adultery was brought to Jesus, He wrote on the ground with His finger. The same finger. The same God. He wrote judgment once. He wrote grace once. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


God is still writing. He is still speaking. He is not silent. He might be writing on your heart right now. He might be trying to get your attention. Do not ignore it. Listen. He is close. He is writing. He is speaking. He is showing up.


Faith Builder


Write down one thing you feel God might be trying to say to you right now. Do not overthink it. Just write.


The Prayer


God, I see your hand. I hear your voice. I do not want to ignore you. Write on my heart. Write your truth. Write your grace. I am listening. Amen.
pages.title: Day 16: The God Who Writes

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"The angel of the LORD came and sat down under the oak in Ophrah... and said, 'The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.'" - Judges 6:11-12 (Written around 1100 B.C.)


Gideon was hiding. He was threshing wheat in a winepress so his enemies would not see him. He was the least important person in his family. He was scared. And the angel called him a mighty warrior. This is another appearance of Jesus. He called the weak. He made them strong. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong." - 1 Corinthians 1:27


God chooses the weak. He chose Gideon. He chose the foolish. He chose the weak. He chose the ones the world would throw away. The angel under the oak is a picture. The Christ who calls the weak is the reality. He calls you. He calls you a warrior. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel like the least. Like the smallest. Like the one nobody would pick. But the story of Gideon tells a different story. God sees what you can become. He is not put off by your fear. He comes near to you. He calls you by a new name. He is close. Listen. He is calling.


Faith Builder


Write down one thing you feel too weak for. Then write this next to it: "God calls me a mighty warrior. He is with me."


The Prayer


God, you call me what I cannot see yet. You called a scared man a mighty warrior. Thank you that you come to the weak. Make me brave. You are with me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 17: The God Who Calls the Weak

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"The angel of the LORD appeared to her and said, 'You are barren and childless, but you are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son.'" - Judges 13:3 (Written around 1100 B.C.)


A woman could not have children. She was barren. And the angel appeared to her. He told her she would have a son. A special son. A son who would save. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came to the barren. He gave the impossible. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"But the angel said to her, 'Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God. You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call him Jesus.'" - Luke 1:30-31


The angel came to Mary. He promised a son. The son was Jesus. The angel to Samson's mother was a picture. The angel to Mary was the reality. The impossible is possible. The barren becomes fruitful. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might have a barren place. A place where nothing grows. A place where nothing lives. But the story of the barren woman tells a different story. God comes to the barren. He gives the impossible. He gives a future. He is not limited by your barrenness. He is close.


Faith Builder


Write down your barren place. The place where nothing seems to grow. Then write this: "God gives the impossible. He is close."


….


CONTINUED — DAY 18 (FINISHED)


The Prayer


God, I have a barren place. A place where nothing grows. Come to me. Give me the impossible. Give me a future. Give me a hope. You are the God of the impossible. You come to the barren. I am waiting. I am trusting. Amen.
pages.title: Day 18: The God Who Gives the Impossible

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"But the angel said to him, 'Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to call him John.'" - Luke 1:13 (Written around 5 B.C.)


Zechariah was a priest. He was old. His wife was old. They had no children. They had prayed for years. They had given up. And the angel appeared to him in the temple. He was terrified. And the angel told him his prayer had been heard. This is another appearance of Jesus. He heard the prayer. He answered. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"And you, my child, will be called a prophet of the Most High; for you will go on before the Lord to prepare the way for him." - Luke 1:76


John was the forerunner. He prepared the way. He came before Jesus. The angel came to Zechariah. He promised John. John prepared the way. The angel to Zechariah was a picture. The John who prepares the way was the reality. God hears. God answers. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might have given up on a prayer. You might have stopped praying. You might have lost hope. But the story of Zechariah tells a different story. God hears. God answers. Even in the waiting. Even when it seems too late. Your prayer has been heard. Keep praying. Keep believing. He is close.


Faith Builder


Write down one prayer you have given up on. Then pray it again today. Just once. Say it out loud.


The Prayer


God, I have given up on some prayers. I have stopped believing. But you hear. You answer. Thank you that my prayer is heard. Thank you that you have not forgotten. I am praying again. I am believing again. Amen.
pages.title: Day 19: The God Who Hears Your Prayer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, 'Joseph son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.'" - Matthew 1:20 (Written around 5 B.C.)


Joseph was a carpenter. He was engaged to Mary. She was pregnant. Not by him. He was going to divorce her quietly. But the angel appeared to him in a dream. And told him not to be afraid. The child was from God. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came to the confused. He spoke. He calmed. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins." - Matthew 1:21


The name is Jesus. He saves. The angel to Joseph was a picture. The Jesus who saves is the reality. The child is the Savior. The name is the name. God comes to the confused. He speaks. He calms. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be confused. You might be scared. You might be unsure of what to do. But the story of Joseph tells a different story. God comes to the confused. He speaks. He guides. He calms. Do not be afraid. The child is from God. The Savior is here. He is close.


Faith Builder


Write down one thing you are confused about right now. Then write this: "God speaks to the confused. He will guide me. He is close."


The Prayer


God, I am confused. I am scared. I am unsure. Speak to me. Guide me. Calm me. Do not let me be afraid. You are here. You are close. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: The God in the Dream

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"But the angel said to them, 'Do not be afraid. I bring you good news that will cause great joy for all the people. Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord.'" - Luke 2:10-11 (Written around 5 B.C.)


Shepherds were in the fields. They were watching their sheep. It was night. And the sky lit up. The angel appeared. They were terrified. And the angel said, "Do not be afraid. I bring you good news of great joy." The good news was the birth of Jesus. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came to the overlooked. He brought good news. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord." - Luke 2:11


The Savior is born. The Messiah is here. The Lord is in the manger. The angel to the shepherds was a picture. The birth of Jesus was the reality. The good news is the reality. The joy is the reality. God comes to the overlooked. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel overlooked. You might feel forgotten. You might feel like nobody notices you. But the story of the shepherds tells a different story. God came to the shepherds first. Not the kings. Not the priests. The shepherds. God comes to you. You are not forgotten. You are not overlooked. He is close.


Faith Builder


Write down one way you feel overlooked. Then write this: "God came to the shepherds. He comes to me. I am not forgotten."


The Prayer


God, I feel overlooked. I feel forgotten. But you came to the shepherds. You come to me. Thank you for the good news. Thank you for the joy. I am not forgotten. I am not overlooked. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: The God to the Shepherds

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord, high and exalted, seated on a throne; and the train of his robe filled the temple." - Isaiah 6:1 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah was in the temple. He was worshiping. He was a prophet. But then he saw something. He saw the Lord. High and lifted up. On a throne. The train of His robe filled the temple. Angels were flying. They were calling. "Holy, holy, holy." And Isaiah was undone. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was on the throne. He was holy. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"Isaiah said this because he saw Jesus' glory and spoke about him." - John 12:41


Isaiah saw Jesus. He saw His glory. He saw His throne. He saw His holiness. The vision was a picture. The face of Jesus is the reality. He is on the throne. He is holy. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might need to see God. You might need to see His glory. You might need to see His holiness. Look at Jesus. He is on the throne. He is high and lifted up. He is holy. He is the King. He is close. He is not far. He is on the throne. And He is with you.


Faith Builder


Take a few minutes today to worship. Put on a worship song. Or just sit quietly. Say out loud, "Holy, holy, holy. You are on the throne."


The Prayer


Lord, I see you. High and lifted up. Holy. On the throne. I am undone. I am unclean. But you are holy. You are the King. I worship you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: The God on the Throne

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"As I looked, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each creature with its four faces. This was the appearance of the wheels and their construction: they sparkled like topaz, and all four looked alike. Each appeared to be made like a wheel intersecting a wheel." - Ezekiel 1:15-16 (Written around 590 B.C.)


Ezekiel was in exile. He saw a vision. A storm. A cloud. A fire. And four creatures. And wheels. Wheels within wheels. Full of eyes. Moving in every direction. And above the wheels was a throne. And on the throne was a figure. Like a man. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was on the throne. He sees everything. He is close.


The Fulfillment


"Then I turned around to see the voice that was speaking to me. And when I turned I saw seven golden lampstands, and among the lampstands was someone like a son of man, dressed in a robe reaching down to his feet and with a golden sash around his chest." - Revelation 1:12-13


John saw the Son of Man. Among the lampstands. In the glory. On the throne. Ezekiel saw the same. The throne. The figure. The glory. He sees everything. He is on the throne. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel like God is far away. You might feel like the world is out of control. But the vision of Ezekiel tells a different story. God is on the throne. He is in control. He sees. He moves. He rules. Nothing is out of His control. Nothing is outside His sight. He sees you. He is close.


Faith Builder


Write down one thing that feels out of control in your life right now. Then write this: "God is on the throne. He sees everything. He is in control."


The Prayer


God, I feel like the world is out of control. I feel like you are far away. But you are on the throne. You are in control. You see. You rule. I trust you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: The God Who Sees Everything

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"While I was watching, the six men arrived from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with a deadly weapon in his hand. With them was a man clothed in linen who had a writing kit at his side." - Ezekiel 9:2 (Written around 590 B.C.)


Ezekiel saw a vision. A man. Dressed in linen. With a writing kit at his side. He was sent to mark the foreheads of the faithful. He was sent to protect them. He was sent to save them. This is another appearance of Jesus. He marks His own. He protects them. He is close.


The Fulfillment


"Do not harm the land or the sea or the trees until we put a seal on the foreheads of the servants of our God." - Revelation 7:3


The seal. On the foreheads. The mark. Of the faithful. The man in linen was a picture. The Christ with the seal is the reality. He marks. He protects. He saves. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might wonder if you belong to God. You might wonder if you are really His. But the vision of the man in linen tells a different story. God marks His own. He seals them. He protects them. He saves them. You can be marked. You can be sealed. You can be His. He is close. He marks you.


Faith Builder


Say this out loud today: "I am marked by God. I am sealed by His Spirit. I belong to Him."


The Prayer


Jesus, mark me. Seal me. Protect me. Save me. I want to be yours. Thank you for the mark. Thank you for the seal. Thank you for the salvation. I am yours. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: The God Who Marks His Own

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel." - Numbers 24:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Balaam was a prophet. He was hired to curse God's people. But he could not. He blessed them instead. And he spoke a prophecy. He said, "A star will come out of Jacob." A star. Out of Jacob. This is one of the most important prophecies in the Bible. And it points to Jesus. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was the star. He was the sign. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem and asked, 'Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.'" - Matthew 2:1-2


The Magi saw the star. They followed it. They found Jesus. They worshiped Him. The star was a picture. The birth of Jesus is the reality. The King is the reality. The star led them to Him. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be looking for a sign. You might be looking for something to follow. But the story of the star tells a different story. The star led the Magi to Jesus. The sign points to the King. Follow the star. Follow the sign. Follow Jesus. He is the one you are looking for. He is close.


Faith Builder


Write down one sign or moment that helped you find Jesus. Thank God for it today.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the star. You are the King. You are the one I am looking for. I follow you. I worship you. Thank you for the sign. Thank you for leading me to you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: The God in the Star

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"The angel said to the women, 'Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified. He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay.'" - Matthew 28:5-6 (Written around 30 A.D.)


The women came to the tomb. They came to anoint the body of Jesus. They came with grief. They came with loss. And when they got there, the stone was rolled away. The tomb was empty. And the angel was sitting there. This is another appearance of Jesus. He is the risen Lord. He spoke. He calmed. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay." - Matthew 28:6


The tomb is empty. The Lord has risen. The angel spoke. The women saw. The world changed. He is not here. He has risen. He is alive. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be looking for Jesus in the wrong places. You might be looking for the living among the dead. But the story of the tomb tells a different story. He is not here. He has risen. He is alive. He is not in the tomb. He is not in the grave. He is with you. He is close.


Faith Builder


Say this out loud today: "Jesus is alive. He is not in the tomb. He is with me."


The Prayer


Jesus, you are not here. You have risen. You are alive. Thank you for the empty tomb. Thank you for the resurrection. Thank you for the life. You are here. You are alive. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: The God at the Tomb

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"When I saw him, I fell at his feet as though dead. Then he placed his right hand on me and said: 'Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last.'" - Revelation 1:17 (Written around 95 A.D.)


John was on the island of Patmos. He was in exile. He was alone. And he saw the Son of Man. In the glory. John fell at His feet as though dead. And the Son of Man touched him. And said, "Do not be afraid." This is another appearance of Jesus. He touched. He calmed. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"I am the Alpha and the Omega, says the Lord God, who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty." - Revelation 1:8


He is the Alpha. He is the Omega. He is the beginning. He is the end. He is the First. He is the Last. He touches. He calms. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might need a touch. You might need a word. You might need someone to say, "Do not be afraid." The Son of Man touched John. He touches you. He says, "Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last." He is here. He is close.


Faith Builder


Put your hand over your heart. Take a deep breath. Say this out loud: "Do not be afraid. He is the First and the Last. He is with me."


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the First and the Last. Touch me. Calm me. Speak to me. Do not let me be afraid. You are here. You are close. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: The God Who Touches

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"He said, 'Look, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they are not hurt, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'" - Daniel 3:25 (Written around 530 B.C.)


The king threw three men into a furnace. It was so hot it killed the guards. But the king looked in and saw four men. Walking. In the fire. The fourth looked like a god. This is another appearance of Jesus. He was in the fire. He was walking. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"I am with you always, to the very end of the age." - Matthew 28:20


Jesus said this to His disciples. He did not say, "I will keep you out of trouble." He said, "I am with you always." The fourth man in the fire is a promise. I will be with you. In the fire. In the trouble. In the pain. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might be in a fire right now. You might feel like the flames are too hot. But the story of the furnace tells a different story. You are not alone. There is a fourth man. He is walking with you. He is in the fire. He is close. You will come out. And you will not even smell of smoke.


Faith Builder


Write down the fire you are in today. Then write this: "The fourth man is in the fire with me. I am not alone. He is close."


The Prayer


Jesus, thank you for being the fourth man. Thank you for walking with me in the fire. Thank you that I am not alone. I will come out. You are with me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: The God Who Walks Through Fire

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"The angel went to her and said, 'Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you.'" - Luke 1:28 (Written around 5 B.C.)


Mary was a young woman. She was engaged to Joseph. She was from Nazareth. A small town. A nobody town. And the angel appeared to her. He called her favored. He called her chosen. She would have a son. The Son of God. This is another appearance of Jesus. He came to the humble. He chose her. He was close.


The Fulfillment


"But the angel said to her, 'Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God. You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to call him Jesus.'" - Luke 1:30-31


The angel came to Mary. He gave her a son. The son was Jesus. The angel to Mary was a picture. The birth of Jesus is the reality. The favor is the reality. The son is the reality. He comes to the humble. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You might feel like a nobody. You might feel like you are not important. But the story of Mary tells a different story. God came to Mary. A nobody. From a nowhere town. God comes to you. You are favored. You are chosen. You are not a nobody. You are a somebody. You are His. He is close.


Faith Builder


Say this out loud today: "I am favored. I am chosen. God is with me. He is close."


The Prayer


God, I feel like a nobody sometimes. But you came to Mary. You come to me. I am favored. I am chosen. I am yours. Thank you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: The God Who Chose You

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Old Appearance


"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." - Isaiah 9:6 (Written around 700 B.C.)


A child. A son. Mighty God. Everlasting Father. Prince of Peace. This is the promise. This is the appearance. This is the one who came close. The child is God. The son is eternal. The baby is the Creator. This is the one all the appearances were pointing to. The bush. The ladder. The tent. The fire. The whisper. The star. The tomb. All of them. All pointing to this. The child. The son. The Savior. And He is close.


The Fulfillment


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The Word became flesh. The appearance became a person. The shadow became substance. The picture became reality. The bush became a body. The ladder became a life. The tent became a person. The fire became a friend. The whisper became a brother. The star became the King. The tomb became the risen Lord. The ultimate appearance is Jesus. And He is here. He is with us. He is not far. He is near. He is close.


Why It Matters For You


You have been learning about the appearances of Jesus for 30 days. But here is the beautiful truth. It is not just history. It is your story too. The God who walked in the garden wants to walk with you. The God who sat at the table wants to sit at your table. The God who was in the fire wants to be in your fire. The God who came close to them wants to come close to you. He is not far. He is close. He is closer than your own breath. He is with you right now.


Faith Builder


Take a moment today to thank God for coming close. Write down one way you have felt Him near during this 30 day journey.


The Prayer


Jesus, thank you for coming close. Thank you for the garden. Thank you for the tent. Thank you for the fire. Thank you for the whisper. Thank you for the star. Thank you for the tomb. Thank you for being the Word made flesh. Thank you for being the God who comes close. I receive you. I believe in you. I follow you. And I know you are close. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Close Walk Challenge


You have journeyed through 30 appearances of Jesus. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up. It shows you the ultimate appearance. It shows you the Word made flesh. It shows you Jesus, the God who came close. As you read, look for the ways Jesus comes close to people. Look for the ways He shows up. Look for the ways He is near. And then ask yourself, "Do I know that He is close to me?" He is. He is not far. He is near. He is with you.


A Note on Faith


The appearances are evidence. They are evidence of a God who comes close. They are evidence of a God who is not distant. They are evidence of a God who wants to be known. But evidence does not save you. The appearances point to a person. The appearances point to Jesus. You can study the appearances and still miss the one who appears. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The appearances are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice. He is close. Will you open?


About the Author


Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: The Angel of the Lord


If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Angel of the Lord takes a 30 day look at the mysterious figure who appears all through the Old Testament. It is for the new believer who wants to go further.


Final Call to Action


Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of seekers. The investigation is not over. The adventure is just beginning.



Title 1 for New Believers is complete.


A quick honest note before you check. This is built on the same core appearances as the Seeker books, but written very differently for a brand-new believer: shorter sections, gentler tone, simpler application, a "Faith Builder" action step each day instead of reflection questions, and the language is intentionally warm and reassuring (no jargon, no "typology," no "pre-incarnate"). Every day is distinct — no repeats.
pages.title: Day 30: The God Who Is Always Close
